reason: A second, different value for a PROV attribute raises `ProvException` with `Cannot have more than one value for attribute <attr>` and stores nothing, whether the call has a collection pair, a `None` collection, a string collection name, no collection, one-shot iteration, an earlier call or a derivation. #700 and spec 5 section 4.2: the single-value rule holds for every PROV attribute of every record type with no `prov:collection` lift.

A read through an accessor, a property, `unified()`, `flattened()`, the graph and dot converters or a writer leaves the keys of every record's `_attributes` as they were. #696 and spec 5 section 4.1: a read creates no attribute entry.

A second, different `prov:time` on a generation raises `ProvException` and leaves the `_attributes` keys and `attributes` as they were. Spec 5 section 4.1 (#696) and 4.2 (#700): a rejected value is not stored and a call that stores nothing changes nothing.

On a fresh entity `get_asserted_types()` equals `set()` and is falsy, `.value` equals `set()` and `.label` is `"ex:e"`. The #34 row of `docs/upgrading-3.0.md` (2.x return types), and the `label` fallback to the identifier text. No source found for the label fallback.

Removed. After `set_time(startTime=...)` the attribute entry of the record had the type name `TypedValueSet` and `get_startTime()` returned the time. The classifier gave rewrite, because the test pinned the private class name `TypedValueSet`. The maintainer sent it through the layers as a removal, and #34 does not describe its input, since #34 is about extra attribute values such as `2` and `2.0`. test_extras.py::test_use_set_time_helpers takes over the storage type, because it compares a `set_time` activity with one built with `startTime=` and `endTime=` and so reaches `value_keys()` on both containers through `ProvBundle.__eq__`, `ProvRecord.__hash__` and `ProvRecord._typed_attributes`. test_model.py::test_activity_set_time_start_only takes over the start-only `get_startTime()` line. The verifier and the judge planted faults in `ProvActivity.set_time` (a plain set or a plain list in place of `TypedValueSet`, and a plain set on the start branch alone) and each failed test_extras.py::test_use_set_time_helpers with an AttributeError from `TypedValueSet.value_keys`. Storing the start only when an end is given failed test_model.py::test_activity_set_time_start_only, and swapping the keys failed it, test_model.py::test_activity_set_time_both and test_model.py::test_activity_set_time_end_only. The mutation run over records.py left no mutant undetected.

The verifier's three faults in `ProvRecord.add_asserted_type` (store the first only, overwrite, store to a copy) each failed the takeover, the removed test owned no arc, and the mutation run left no mutant undetected.

It is now the `bool-and-int` row of test_attribute_merging.py::test_construction_retains_differently_typed_values, with the same input and the same assertion. An entity built with two values on one attribute keeps both, read back through `attributes` with their types, for the pairs `(2, 2.0)`, `(1, True)` and `(2, True)` (rows `int-and-float`, `bool-and-int` and `int-and-unequal-bool`). #34: attribute sets used to drop a Python-equal but differently typed value, and the module docstring names construction as one of the places it happened. The row `int-and-unequal-bool` is the control pair, because `2 != True` and so it never collapsed. Merged from test_attribute_merging.py::test_construction_retains_python_equal_differently_typed_values, test_attribute_merging.py::test_construction_retains_bool_vs_int and test_attribute_merging.py::test_int_vs_bool_that_are_not_equal_is_not_a_regression_case, which differed only in value pair and expected set. Every input and the one assertion stay, with no branch on a parameter. The merge check showed identical arcs per row in `TypedValueSet.add` and `_value_key`, and the mutation run over records.py and _values.py changed no mutant's status. The judge renamed the merged function from test_attribute_merging.py::test_construction_retains_python_equal_differently_typed_values, because the `int-and-unequal-bool` row is not a Python-equal pair.

Two entities with the same typed values on `ex:v` and `ex:w`, asserted in opposite order, are equal and hash alike. #34: the typed-value comparison must still ignore the order of assertion.
An entity built with `("ex:v", 2)` twice holds the single value `2`. #34: only Python-equal values of different types stay apart, a true duplicate still collapses.

`get_asserted_types()` after two `add_asserted_type` calls returns an instance of set equal to the two names. The maintainer decision in the module docstring and the #34 row of `docs/upgrading-3.0.md`: `ProvRecord.get_asserted_types` keeps its 2.x return type. It took over `test_attribute_merging.py::test_add_asserted_type_mutates_live_storage_not_a_copy`, which made the same two `ProvRecord.add_asserted_type` calls on a fresh entity and asserted only a length of 2, which this test's `== {foo, bar}` implies. The verifier planted three faults in `ProvRecord.add_asserted_type` (store only the first type, overwrite, store to a copy), and each failed this test with the removed test deselected.

Adding `999` to the set returned by `get_attribute("ex:v")` leaves a later `get_attribute("ex:v")` equal to `{2}`. The #34 row of `docs/upgrading-3.0.md`: the accessors return a copy that no longer writes through.

`get_attribute("ex:v")` on a record holding `2` and `2.0` returns an instance of set equal to `{2}`. The maintainer decision in the module docstring and the #34 row of `docs/upgrading-3.0.md`: `get_attribute()` keeps its 2.x return type.

Two entities with one identifier, one holding `2` and `2.0` on `ex:v` and the other holding `2`, have `attributes` of length 2 and 1, are unequal and hash differently. #34: record equality and hashing must see the retained typed values. It took over `test_attribute_merging.py::test_records_with_different_retained_value_sets_are_not_equal`, which built the same two entities from the same identifier and asserted the same inequality and hash inequality, without the `attributes` lengths. The verifier planted four faults in `ProvRecord.__eq__` and `ProvRecord.__hash__` (comparing `frozenset(self.attributes)`, comparing attribute names only, and dropping the attribute term from the hash), and each failed this test as well as the removed one. `ProvRecord._typed_attributes` is the typed comparison they bypass.

Removed. An entity built with `2` and `True` on one attribute kept both, read back through `attributes` with their types; `2 != True`, so the pair never collapsed (#34). It is now the `int-and-unequal-bool` row of test_attribute_merging.py::test_construction_retains_differently_typed_values, with the same input, the same assertion and its comment. The merge check showed identical arcs for the row in `TypedValueSet.add` and `_value_key`, and the mutation run over records.py and _values.py changed no mutant's status.

On the record's own per-attribute container holding `2` and `2.0`, membership finds each, `3` is absent, `discard(2.0)` leaves only `2` and `discard(3)` changes nothing, so `TypedValueSet.__contains__` and `TypedValueSet.discard` key on `_value_key` as `TypedValueSet.add` does (#34). No public call reaches `TypedValueSet.discard`. The judge ran the whole suite with both methods wrapped to record their callers, and only this test calls `discard`. This test alone checks the type-aware membership of `TypedValueSet.__contains__`, because test_attribute_merging.py::test_unpickled_value_set_from_an_earlier_release_is_rekeyed calls it with an int only. The maintainer accepted the query. A separate change bases `TypedValueSet` on collections.abc.Set, deletes `discard` and cuts this test to its membership lines.

Two `xsd:decimal` literals `"10"` and `"10.00"` on one attribute leave one value, and it is the first one asserted. #77: decimal literals compare by value, and the first value asserted is the one kept.

`Literal("hi", langtag="en")` and `Literal("hi", langtag="EN")` on one attribute leave one value, and its tag is `en`. #259: language tags compare case-insensitively, and the first value asserted is the one kept.

A document with `2` and `2.0` on one attribute equals its reload from JSON, XML and RDF, and the reloaded record holds both typed values. #34: the retained values must survive serialization round trips.

A record that was read before extra attributes were added serialises to PROV-JSON, PROV-JSONLD and PROV-N identically to one never read, with attributes in assertion order. #696 and spec 5 section 4.1: output key order follows the order values were asserted.

Removed. Two entities with one identifier, one holding `2` and `2.0` on `ex:v` and the other holding `2`, are unequal and hash differently (#34). test_attribute_merging.py::test_hash_distinguishes_typed_values_even_when_attributes_property_collapses takes over, because it builds the same two entities and asserts the same inequality and hash inequality, plus the `attributes` lengths. The verifier's four faults in `ProvRecord.__eq__` and `ProvRecord.__hash__` failed the takeover as well, the removed test owned no arc, and the mutation run left no mutant undetected.

After `add_attributes([("ex:v", 2.0)])` on an entity that holds `2`, `attributes` shows both `(int, 2)` and `(float, 2.0)`. #34: the module docstring names separate `add_attributes()` calls as one of the three input shapes.

`unified()` on two same-identifier entities with different `prov:startTime` extra attributes raises `ProvException` and not `ProvUnificationError`. #253 and the maintainer ruling in the test: the single-value guard predates the unification work and stays a plain `ProvException`.

Two same-identifier entities asserting `2` and `2.0` on `ex:v` unify to one record that holds both values. #34: the module docstring names `unified()`'s extra-attribute union as one of the three input shapes.

A value set loaded from 3.2.x state holding a raw `Identifier` value writes in PROV-N as an `xsd:anyURI` literal that reads back as `Literal("http://example.org/x", XSD_ANYURI)`. #658: a raw `Identifier` value from an old pickle must still write as `xsd:anyURI`.

A value set rebuilt through `__setstate__` from the 3.2.x state `{(int, 5): 5}` contains `5`, iterates as `[5]` and equals the live container. `HISTORY.md` says `Identifier`, `QualifiedName`, `Namespace` and `Literal` load pickles written by earlier releases, and the 3.3.0 how-to says a `Literal` is checked on load from a pickle of an earlier release. No source found for the value set itself.

`.value` on a record holding `prov:value` `2` and `2.0` returns an instance of set equal to `{2}`. The maintainer decision in the module docstring and the #34 row of `docs/upgrading-3.0.md`: `.value` keeps its 2.x return type.
